title: Detached maintenance must release its Node event-loop reference
summary: A detached OS process can still retain its parent's Node event loop. Release only explicitly background, ignored-stdio child handles after managed registration and prove natural exit.
reusable_steps: A detached OS process can still retain its parent's Node event loop
Release only explicitly background, ignored-stdio child handles after managed registration and prove natural exit
expected_outcome: When a one-shot check prints success but does not exit, distinguish output correctness from process lifetime. Inspect owned child handles before changing deadlines or golden baselines. For intentionally detached maintenance with ignored stdio, call child.unref() after spawnManagedProcess has registered supervision; preserve registration failure handling, submission markers and asynchronous job behavior. Do not globally unref managed children: watch and manual execution owners may require their handles. Use a finite timer-only child through the real compiled managed-process module: referenced control retains ProcessWrap and exits after child completion; released variant has no ProcessWrap and naturally exits while child exitCode is null. Avoid forced process.exit and wall-clock thresholds. Register any new boundary-test consumer and run strict state checks without overlapping runtime writers. This mechanism is proven by a controlled fixture; the original failed CI runner's child PID was not recovered.
